title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a fragment from Grothendieck's 1965 notes on the Galois theory of motives. It sits among unrelated pages of a Bourbaki draft (n° 413, distributions ponctuelles), so it is a loose sheet. Almost the whole lower half is struck through, so the reading is necessarily partial.

(1) Opening statement. 'Si xi est réelle, [la réalisation] a une structure de Hodge à involution.' The most plausible reading: xi is an embedding of the base field K into C, i.e. an archimedean place. Each such place gives a Betti/Hodge realization of a motive. If xi is real, complex conjugation acts on the realization (Deligne's later F_infinity), giving a Hodge structure with an involution compatible with the Hodge decomposition (h^{pq} goes to h^{qp}). This is what later became 'real Hodge structures with F_infinity' or Hodge structures over R.

(2) Question and diagram. Grothendieck asks 'Comment se réalisent ces structures de Hodge ??' and sketches a factorization:
- M_o-bar (a category of motives, probably over K or a subcategory such as CM/abelian motives) maps by a fibre functor 'foncteur xi' to G^o-Modules. Here G^o is a group scheme, perhaps the identity component of the motivic Galois group, or a torus in the CM case. 'Variété' was crossed out and replaced by 'G^o-Modules', suggesting he passed from a geometric to a group-theoretic (Tannakian) description.
- A further functor Phi_xi takes G^o-modules to 'Réseaux de Hodge', i.e. Hodge structures with an integral lattice.
- A second embedding xi' gives a parallel functor 'foncteur xi''. Both appear 'définis sur K-tilde provenant de K' (K-tilde probably a Galois closure or extension of K), with a comparison Phi.
In modern terms: the Hodge realization attached to a complex place should factor through representations of the motivic group, via a cocharacter (Hodge/Deligne torus to G), and one wants to compare realizations at different embeddings.

(3) Crossed-out attempts. Fragments mention K^*, the norm N_{K^*/Q}, 'K^*-modules', 'Si E^o ≠ 0', 'K^* opère ... par Z', and 'longueur variable'. These look like a try at the CM/torus case, where the group is a quotient of Res_{K/Q} G_m with norm conditions (the Serre-group/Weil-number picture). The deleted end defines, for a G^o-module V:
- V tensor_Q C with a Hodge structure T_xi^V (cf. a basis of the K_i);
- a K-tilde-vector space H_xi^V.
That is, a Hodge realization plus a de Rham-type rational structure attached to the place xi.

Purpose: to understand how Hodge realizations, and their dependence on the complex embedding, are encoded in the Tannakian description of motives. This is a precursor of Deligne's Hodge-theoretic formalism in 'Valeurs de fonctions L' (1979) and of the Serre/Taniyama group picture for CM motives.
errors: No outright mathematical errors can be assessed; the page is a sketch with most of the content struck out.

The definition of H_xi^V as a K-tilde-vector space attached to an abstract G^o-module is unexplained. One would need extra structure (a cocharacter, or a rational structure over the reflex/Galois field) to produce it, so it is a gap rather than a construction.

ideas.what: For a real embedding of the base field, the Hodge realization carries an involution (complex conjugation / F_infinity)
ideas.modern_name: Real Hodge structures with F_infinity; Hodge realization at real places
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II 1971; Valeurs de fonctions L 1979)
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted at in Grothendieck's discussions of motives (letters to Serre, 1964-65); not in a standard published text to my knowledge

ideas.what: Hodge realizations factor as motives -> G^o-modules (fibre functor) -> Hodge structures, depending on the choice of complex embedding xi
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian formalism; Hodge realization via a cocharacter of the motivic Galois group; dependence of Betti realization on the embedding
ideas.where_published: Récoltes et Semailles mentions the motivic Galois group in general terms only

ideas.what: Crossed-out attempt involving K^*, N_{K^*/Q} and K^*-modules, apparently a torus/CM-type description of the group
ideas.modern_name: Serre group / Weil restriction tori for CM motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre 1968 (Abelian l-adic representations), Deligne, Langlands, Milne-Shih (Taniyama group)

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1965 explicitly posed how Hodge realizations at different complex (and real) embeddings arise from the representation category of the motivic group, and flagged the Hodge structure with involution at real places. This anticipates Deligne's F_infinity formalism, but the page is too fragmentary to contain a result.
missed.quote: Si ξ réelle, — a une structure de Hodge à involution. Comment se réalisent ces structures de Hodge ??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents early Grothendieck thinking on embedding-dependence of Hodge realizations and on real Hodge structures within the Tannakian picture. These topics were later developed by Deligne, Milne-Shih and others.

deep.surprise_reason: A historically interesting but very fragmentary sketch whose mathematical content (Hodge realizations through a fibre functor, involution at real places, a torus picture for CM) was developed and credited later. Nothing here is a finished result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Variété' is crossed out and replaced by 'G^o-Modules' in the first arrow's target.
'Réseaux de Hodge' appears correct as the target of Phi_xi (lattices with Hodge structure).
The left column likely reads 'M̄_o / réalisés[?] / définis sur K̃ provenant de K'; the second arrow is labelled 'foncteur ξ'' (with prime), and Phi has no subscript.
The lower block is crossed out with diagonal strokes; the readings 'K^*-modules', 'N_{K^*/Q}', 'T_ξ^V' and 'H_ξ^V' are plausible.
